checks: The existing ordinary profile inequality applies to the full-dimensional K and this D+1-cap cover for each α>0. For every cap with A_i>α, a finite distal threshold removes exactly A_i−α by continuity and hyperplane nullity.

The trimmed intersection K′ has mass at least α/γ and each old cap retains at most α. Its covered maximum normalized depth is at most α/|K′|, so ordinary depth rigidity forces equality in volume and makes K′ a simplex. The union bound is then tight and the removed pieces have pairwise zero-volume overlap.

Every cap containing the centroid of K′ has mass α. If the centroid were strictly inside that cap, a positive-volume interior slab could be removed before reaching its through-centroid cap, whose mass is still at least α. Thus the equality-direction result applies to the original plane and orientation.

A proper subset of the canonical directions fails to cover any neighborhood of the centroid by barycentric increments of sum zero and negative entries on the selected indices. Hence all D+1 original caps are distinct and canonical, even if empty or repeated caps were permitted initially.

A positive removed piece contains an interior point strictly below every other retained plane. The segment from the centroid crosses its cutting plane with all other inequalities strict, producing a genuine (D−1)-facet. Its canonical outward normal can expose only one vertex, a contradiction for D≥2.

The converse and α=a specialization follow from the canonical vertex homothety and from removing the positive part at the minimum. The proof matches 3bb0f1835a5838c5:01 §§1–4 including the positive-level profile extension.

dependencies.hypotheses: Its ordinary-volume clause applies to the stated full-dimensional compact convex body and finite nonzero-normal covering caps at α>0.

Its hypothesis is a concurrent cap cover of all ambient space with every cap budget at most γ|K|, whereas these input caps need only cover K and can initially have unrelated offsets and cap masses. The trimming and equality argument identifies the exact originals.
